event.title: Preschool Program: Alla Hjärtans Dag
event.description:
ASI’s Preschool Program creates opportunities for families to experience Swedish art, culture, and traditions together. Join us in February to explore Alla Hjärtans Dag.

Preschoolers and their important grown-ups discover how Swedish families celebrate Alla Hjärtans Dag, or “All Hearts’ Day,” during this special morning at ASI. Through stories, crafts, and hands-on activities, children explore how people in Sweden use this day to show care and appreciation for the people they love. Together, preschoolers and their important grown-ups explore questions like, “How do Swedish families celebrate Alla Hjärtans Dag?” and “Why do they celebrate it?”

Children will create a special craft, taste Swedish candy, and explore the Castle while discovering the traditions behind this heartwarming holiday. ASI educators guide preschoolers and their important grown-ups through a playful introduction to Swedish culture, encouraging curiosity, creativity, and connection. event.title: Nordic Book Circle
event.description:
Contemporary Nordic literature is full of diverse literary voices, styles, and genres. This September 2026 through May 2027 the ASI Nordic Book Circle will gather monthly, in-person, to read and discuss a work of Nordic literature in English translation. Our focus this year will be on works of literature written by women authors from across the Nordic world. The works we read will chronologically trace books penned between 1912 and 2020, and include two winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature; authors from the countries of Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Greenland; various genres; and a range of topics and perspectives.

If you love to read and discuss literature and would like to expand your appreciation of literature from various parts of the world (the Nordic world in particular), we would love to have you join! Limited to 20 attendees; please register in advance.

2026-2027 Nordic Book Circle titles
September: Kristin Lavransdotter, Book I: The Wreath (1912), by Sigrid Undset, translated from Norwegian by Tiina Nunnally (Penguin Editions, 336 pages), Norway – September 27, 2026

October: The Phantom Carriage (1912), by Selma Lagerlöf, translated from Swedish by Peter Graves (Norvik Press, 124 pages) (Sweden) – October 25, 2026

November: Quicksand (1928) by Nella Larsen (Penguin Classics, 192 pages) (Denmark) – November 22, 2026

December: Kallocain (1940), Karin Boye, translated from Swedish by David McDuff (Penguin Classics, 192 pages) (Sweden) – December 20, 2026

January: Girl Upon Heaven’s Pier (1951), by Eeva-Liisa Manner, translated from Finnish by Terhi Kuusisto (Dalkey Archive Press, 104 pages) (Finland) – January 31, 2027

February: Nothing to be Rescued (1961), by Ásta Sigurðardóttir, translated from Icelandic by Meg Matich (Nordisk Books, 192 pages) Iceland – February 28, 2027

March: Light, Grass, and Letter in April (1962, 1963, 1979), by Inger Christensen, translated from Danish by Susanna Nied (New Directions Publishing, 144 pages) (Denmark) – March 21, 2027

April: Zombieland (2015), by Sørine Steenholdt, translated from Greenlandic to Danish by Niviaq Korneliussen and from Danish to English by Charlotte Barslund (Norvik Press, 150 pages) (Greenland) – April 25, 2027

May: Strega (2020), by Johanna Lykke Holm, translated from Swedish by Saskia Vogel (Riverhead Books, 208 pages) (Sweden) – May 23, 2027

event.title: FIKA Supper Club Concert Series: Wingra Wind Quintet
event.description:
Dive deeper into the world of Nordic classical music with University of Wisconsin-Madison’s faculty ensemble, Wingra Wind Quintet. This group featuring flute, oboe, clarinet, horn and bassoon will present works by Nordic composers. Founded in 1965, the Wingra Wind Quintet is one of the longest-running quintets in the nation. Known for artistic and pedagogical excellence, the ensemble has consistently presented concerts and workshops around the globe to rave reviews.

The FIKA Supper Club series brings Nordic-inflected folk, jazz and classical artists to ASI. Optionally, guests may enjoy extended dinner hours at FIKA Café before the concert, then step into Larson Hall for a musical treat beginning at 7 pm. Don’t miss these nights of musical and culinary delight!

Additional information:

  • Limited dinner reservations and a cash bar are available from 4-7 pm. To reserve your table, email fika@asimn.org.

  • NEW this season: purchase a FIKA Supper Club Season Package for $175 ($150 ASI member). Join us for 6 terrific Nordic-inflected folk, jazz, and classical music concerts for the price of 5! This option is available at checkout through October 16.

The works we read will chronologically trace books penned between 1912 and 2020, and include two winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature; authors from the countries of Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Greenland; various genres; and a range of topics and perspectives.

If you love to read and discuss literature and would like to expand your appreciation of literature from various parts of the world (the Nordic world in particular), we would love to have you join! Limited to 20 attendees; please register in advance.

2026-2027 Nordic Book Circle titles
September: Kristin Lavransdotter, Book I: The Wreath (1912), by Sigrid Undset, translated from Norwegian by Tiina Nunnally (Penguin Editions, 336 pages), Norway – September 27, 2026

October: The Phantom Carriage (1912), by Selma Lagerlöf, translated from Swedish by Peter Graves (Norvik Press, 124 pages) (Sweden) – October 25, 2026

November: Quicksand (1928) by Nella Larsen (Penguin Classics, 192 pages) (Denmark) – November 22, 2026

December: Kallocain (1940), Karin Boye, translated from Swedish by David McDuff (Penguin Classics, 192 pages) (Sweden) – December 20, 2026

January: Girl Upon Heaven’s Pier (1951), by Eeva-Liisa Manner, translated from Finnish by Terhi Kuusisto (Dalkey Archive Press, 104 pages) (Finland) – January 31, 2027

February: Nothing to be Rescued (1961), by Ásta Sigurðardóttir, translated from Icelandic by Meg Matich (Nordisk Books, 192 pages) Iceland – February 28, 2027

March: Light, Grass, and Letter in April (1962, 1963, 1979), by Inger Christensen, translated from Danish by Susanna Nied (New Directions Publishing, 144 pages) (Denmark) – March 21, 2027

April: Zombieland (2015), by Sørine Steenholdt, translated from Greenlandic to Danish by Niviaq Korneliussen and from Danish to English by Charlotte Barslund (Norvik Press, 150 pages) (Greenland) – April 25, 2027

May: Strega (2020), by Johanna Lykke Holm, translated from Swedish by Saskia Vogel (Riverhead Books, 208 pages) (Sweden) – May 23, 2027

event.title: Musically Speaking Lecture Series: The Planets & Beyond
event.description:
Musically Speaking: The Planets and Beyond

Wednesday, September 30, 2026

6pm-7pm

The Powerhouse (Durango)

This is a FREE event.

Light Snacks and Cash Bar available.

Prepare to explore the universe through music! Join the San Juan Symphony’s own Maestro Thomas Heuser for Musically Speaking: The Planets and Beyond, an engaging lecture that takes audiences behind the music of our Season 41 opener.

Discover the stories, ideas, and musical inspiration behind Gustav Holst’s iconic The Planets, along with John Adams’ thrilling Short Ride in a Fast Machine and Mélanie Bonis’ evocative Le Songe de Cléopâtre. Learn more about the composers, the music, and the connections between these works before experiencing them live with the San Juan Symphony.

Whether you’re a longtime classical music lover or simply curious to hear music in a new way, Musically Speaking offers an entertaining and accessible introduction to the upcoming weekend’s program.

event.title: The Planets & Beyond- Durango
event.description:
The Planets & Beyond

10.03.26 | 7:30PM

Community Concert Hall, Durango

SJS Chamber Singers, Amy Barrett, director

Durango Women’s Choir, Rhonda Muckerman, director

San Juan Symphony

Thomas Heuser, conductor

    John Adams, Short Ride in a Fast Machine

    Mélanie Bonis, Le Songe de Cléopâtre, Op. 165

    Gustav Holst, The Planets (1914-1916)

Fasten your seatbelts for a concert of epic proportions! American composer John Adams slings the orchestra into high gear with his brilliant Short Ride in a Fast Machine, which propels us into Gustav Holst’s The Planets – a grand tour of the solar system. From Jupiter the Bringer of Jollity to Mars the Warrior and the wonderfully abstract Neptune, the music depicts Holst’s unique interpretations of each larger-than-life astrological character. Maestro Heuser and the San Juan Symphony will be joined by members of the SJS Chamber Singers and the Durango Women’s Chorus for this impactful musical experience. Our audiences will also be introduced to Mélanie Bonis, a rarely performed French avante-garde composer whose life and music are brimming with energy and drama. Her evocative tone poem, Le Songe de Cléopatre, is part of the huge orchestral triptych Trois Femmes de légende. Expect to be awash in incredible harmonies and the richness of this unusually massive orchestra.

Henderson Fine Arts Center, Farmington

SJS Chamber Singers, Amy Barrett, director

Durango Women’s Choir, Rhonda Muckerman, director

San Juan Symphony

Thomas Heuser, conductor

 

    John Adams, Short Ride in a Fast Machine

    Mélanie Bonis, Le Songe de Cléopâtre, Op. 165

    Gustav Holst, The Planets (1914-1916)

Fasten your seatbelts for a concert of epic proportions! American composer John Adams slings the orchestra into high gear with his brilliant Short Ride in a Fast Machine, which propels us into Gustav Holst’s The Planets – a grand tour of the solar system. From Jupiter the Bringer of Jollity to Mars the Warrior and the wonderfully abstract Neptune, the music depicts Holst’s unique interpretations of each larger-than-life astrological character. Maestro Heuser and the San Juan Symphony will be joined by members of the SJS Chamber Singers and the Durango Women’s Chorus for this impactful musical experience. Our audiences will also be introduced to Mélanie Bonis, a rarely performed French avante-garde composer whose life and music are brimming with energy and drama. Her evocative tone poem, Le Songe de Cléopatre, is part of the huge orchestral triptych Trois Femmes de légende. Expect to be awash in incredible harmonies and the richness of this unusually massive orchestra.

Step into the passionate world of Romantic-era music with the San Juan Symphony’s Musically Speaking: Romantic Giants. This engaging lecture with Maestro Heuser explores the stories, musical ideas, and larger-than-life emotions behind two masterpieces of the orchestral repertoire: Antonín Dvořák’s beloved Cello Concerto and Johannes Brahms’ powerful Symphony No. 3.

event.description:

Wednesday, March 31, 2027

6pm-7pm

Location TBD

This is a FREE event.

Discover the passion, power, and complexity behind the San Juan Symphony’s season finale, Iron and Ivory.. This engaging  lecture explores the emotional world of two giants of Russian music: Dmitri Shostakovich’s provocative Symphony No. 9 and Sergei Rachmaninoff’s sweeping and deeply expressive Piano Concerto No. 2.

Learn more about the fascinating stories behind these works, Shostakovich’s complicated response to the end of World War II, and the enduring appeal of Rachmaninoff’s beloved concerto. We’ll also take a closer look at guest pianist Norman Krieger, returning to the San Juan Symphony as featured soloist.

Come hear the stories behind the music and prepare for a powerful Season 41 finale filled with grandeur, emotion, and unforgettable orchestral sound.

event.title: Iron & Ivory: Shostakovich & Norman Krieger- Durango
event.description:
Iron & Ivory: Shostakovich & Norman Krieger

04.03.27 | 7:30PM

Community Concert Hall, Durango

Norman Krieger, piano soloist

San Juan Symphony

Thomas Heuser, conductor

     Dimitri Shostakovich, Symphony No. 9 in E-flat Major

     Sergei Rachmaninoff, Piano Concerto No. 2 in C Minor

          Norman Krieger, piano

The great Russian master Sergei Rachmaninoff conveys perhaps more passion and feeling than any other composer in history. His music brings audiences to their feet with abundant enthusiasm every time, and such is always the case for his thrilling Second Piano Concerto. We are delighted to welcome back Norman Krieger as our Guest Artist, one of the most acclaimed pianists of his generation, whose academic credits include the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music, the USC Thornton School of Music, and Durango’s own Fort Lewis College, where he served as Professor for well over a decade. Rachmaninoff’s sentimental artistry will be paired with the seamlessly crafted and highly engaging Ninth Symphony by another titanic figure in Russian musical history: Dimitri Shostakovich. Written in reaction to the Second World War, Shostakovich’s Ninth brims with optimism and energy while delving into a host of deeply personal emotions.

Join us October 2–3 at Steamer 10 Theatre for the 11th Annual New York State International Film Festival, a two-day celebration of independent filmmaking from around the world!

Come experience two nights of great short films, meet filmmakers, participate in Q&A discussions, and celebrate independent cinema at the 11th Annual New York State International Film Festival!

event.title: UFF-DA | Sam Licari & The Sweet Tease
event.description:
UFF-DA

Uff-Da — Gritty Blues-Rock with Midwestern Soul
Uff-Da is a powerhouse four-piece blending gritty blues-rock energy with soulful, fuzz-drenched vibes — all rooted in unapologetic Midwestern spirit. Co-fronted by drummer/vocalist Sam McKinney and guitarist/vocalist Chris Marti, with Cody Bruggman on bass and Tim Booth on keys, Uff-Da delivers a sound that’s raw, electric, and impossible to ignore. Formed out of a shared love for sweaty live shows and authentic connection, Uff-Da has carved
a loyal following across the Twin Cities music scene. Their debut self-titled album Uff-Da! is a two-year labor of love, self-produced in a DIY home studio built by the band. The result? A record that punches with raw emotion, catchy hooks, and the kind of musical chemistry you only get when every member pulls equal weight. From local venues to festival stages, Uff-Da brings a live show that’s equal parts gritty blues, powerful rock, and infectious jam sessions — keeping crowds dancing, shouting, and coming back for more. For Uff-Da, it’s not just about the music — it’s about creating momentsthat hit you in the chest and stick with you long after the last chord rings out.

Sam Licari & The Sweet Tease 

Sam Licari and the Sweet Tease is a project by multi instrumentalist and singer/songwriter, Sam Licari. Minnesota born and bred, the versatile Sam Licari has performed with many acts around the Midwest, most notably as the bassist for Minneapolis based reggae-rock group Irie Minds , as well as Alexander Craig , Trent Romens Band, Russ Parrish & The Lone Oaks, Brother Jon Band, Red Eye Ruby, Derek Callendar and the Billytown Wranglers, Love Squad, Cupa Joe and the Sweet Cream, Matt Schatza Trio, and more. Combining his experience with a love for funk, reggae, and blues, Sam has blended them in this unique expression that is all his own, which you can hear on his debut self-titled album and his new EP Done Losin’.

Get ready for a night of gritty blues-rock, soulful grooves, funk, reggae, and Midwestern swagger when Uff-Da and Sam Licari & The Sweet Tease take over the Day Block Brewing Tap Room on Thursday, October 1st from 7–10 PM.

Minneapolis-based Uff-Da brings a raw, high-energy blend of blues-rock, fuzz-drenched guitar, soulful vocals, and infectious jams. With Sam McKinney on drums and vocals, Chris Marti on guitar and vocals, Cody Bruggman on bass, and Tim Booth on keys, the four-piece delivers the kind of sweaty, electric live show built for dancing, shouting along, and losing yourself in the music. Their DIY spirit and powerful chemistry make every performance feel spontaneous and alive.

Opening the night, Sam Licari & The Sweet Tease bring a groove-heavy mix of funk, reggae, blues, and rock. A veteran of the Midwest music scene, Licari’s multi-instrumental background shines through in a sound that’s soulful, rhythmic, and full of personality.

The Tap Room at Day Block Brewing sets the perfect backdrop for the evening, with cold craft beer on tap, great food, and a laid-back Minneapolis atmosphere where the music takes center stage. Grab a pint, order some food, settle in with friends, and let the grooves take over.

Expect a night filled with big guitars, deep grooves, soulful vocals, funky rhythms, bluesy jams, dancing, and plenty of Midwestern good times. Come hungry, come thirsty, and come ready to turn it up.

event.title: Twin Citizen | Dan Bullard | Holly XO
event.description:
Twin Citizen 

Twin Citizen is a four-piece indie rock band out of Saint Paul, Minnesota. Funk, alternative, synth, and progressive textures run underneath songs built to connect, the kind you feel in your chest in a packed room. Adam Lifto calls it “Organic Atari Music.” Joe Hartley puts it a different way: Radiohead and the Red Hot Chili Peppers covering Pink Floyd. However you describe it, every song still sounds like Twin Citizen. The band came together in 2021 chasing one idea: make music that is honest and a little adventurous, then play it like it matters. They have shared stages across the Twin Cities and earned features in Woodbury Magazine, Voyage Minnesota, and more. Right now they are heads-down on their most ambitious work yet, a self-recorded, self-produced full-length tracked in a studio they built themselves. New singles are on the way, with the record targeted for 2027.

Dan Bullard

Dan has been active in the Twin Cities music scene since the age of 9 and is a founding member of instrumental post rock band Trellis which debuted in 2025. The band has been building a following in the Minneapolis alternative music scene with its unique blend of post rock, post metal, desert rock, progressive rock, and psychedelic rock. Highlights so far include multiple shows at Art-A-Whirl and the opportunity to perform with underground greats such as Surrounded By Water, The Color of Cyan, PRGRPHS, North Innsbruck, and Moonlit Mushroom. The band’s debut album will release on 12/5/26 and they will perform an album release show at Day Block Brewery on that date with friends VIN, PRGRPHS, and Surrounded By Water.

In 2026, Dan decided to form a solo project as an alternative outlet where he could blend elements of indie rock, emo, pop punk, pop rock, and “happy post rock.” All instruments and vocals on the project’s debut album were performed by Dan Bullard, and it will be released in 2027. The project will make its live debut at a show on 10/2/26 featuring Twin Citizen and Holly XO at Day Block Brewery with Dan Bullard on vocals and guitar, Joe Marxen (formerly of Loser Magnet) on guitar, Andrew Valentine (of Leslie) on drums, and Nick Stalls on bass.

Holly XO

St. Paul singer-songwriter Holly XO creates poetic, artful music that blends personal experience with themes of healing, strength, spirituality, and hope. Her work carries a thoughtful feminist perspective without preaching, inviting listeners to reflect, connect, and find meaning in their own experiences. Currently working on her debut album, Dear Holly, Holly XO is developing a distinctive artistic voice rooted in vulnerability, resilience, and emotional honesty. The album is slated for release in 2026.

Indie Rock Night at Day Block Brewing

Spend your Friday night with Twin Citizen, Dan Bullard, and Holly XO at Day Block Brewing on Friday, October 2nd, inside the Tap Room. Expect an intimate evening of adventurous songwriting, atmospheric sounds, and heartfelt performances, paired with fresh craft beer, good food, and the laid-back energy of a Minneapolis brewery.

Twin Citizen, a four-piece from St. Paul, blends indie rock with funk, alternative, synth, and progressive textures. Their songs are built for connection—music that can move from atmospheric and adventurous to energetic and groove-driven. They describe their sound as “Organic Atari Music,” while another comparison imagines Radiohead and Red Hot Chili Peppers covering Pink Floyd. However you describe it, Twin Citizen has developed a sound distinctly their own.

Dan Bullard brings his new solo project to the stage for its live debut. Drawing from indie rock, emo, pop punk, pop rock, and what he calls “happy post rock,” Dan creates music that balances emotion with an uplifting sense of movement. After years in the Twin Cities music scene and as a member of Trellis, this new project offers another side of his musical creativity.

Holly XO, a St. Paul singer-songwriter, rounds out the evening with poetic and deeply personal music exploring healing, strength, spirituality, hope, and emotional honesty. Her thoughtful songwriting invites listeners into a reflective and intimate space.

Grab a craft beer, order some food, settle into the Tap Room, and enjoy a night where the atmosphere is as much about connection as it is about the music.

Twin Citizen • Dan Bullard • Holly XO
Friday, October 2nd
Day Block Brewing – Tap Room
Minneapolis, MN

event.title: Inaara | VVakefield | Gradience | Gauze
event.description:
Inaara

Inaara is a metal band bringing a dark, intense, and emotionally charged sound to the modern heavy music scene. Their music combines crushing riffs, powerful rhythms, and story-driven songwriting, with influences ranging from theatrical metal to emotionally raw post-hardcore. The band released their five-song EP Manifest in 2025, featuring tracks including “Death/Rebirth,” “Reduced to Nothing,” and “Pain and Suffering.” With an emphasis on pushing their music as far as possible, Inaara delivers an energetic and uncompromising live experience.

VVakefield

VVakefield is a Minneapolis-based melodic hardcore band delivering a powerful mix of aggressive guitar riffs, driving drums, and melodic vocals. Rooted in the intensity and emotional energy of modern hardcore, their sound balances crushing instrumentation with memorable melodic elements. Known for high-energy live performances, VVakefield brings urgency, passion, and raw intensity to every stage. With music available across major streaming platforms and a growing presence throughout the Minneapolis music scene, VVakefield continues making their mark on melodic hardcore.

Gradience

Minneapolis-based Gradience is a high-energy four-piece rock band blending hard rock, alternative rock, indie, and influences from across the musical spectrum. Formed in 2019, the band has spent years performing throughout the Midwest, developing a reputation for powerful live shows and genre-spanning songwriting. With their album Come What May showcasing tracks including “Sometimes,” “Waiting,” “Comeback,” and “Parasite,” Gradience continues to build its presence in the Twin Cities rock scene with energy, creativity, and an unmistakable sound.

Gauze

Gauze is a Minneapolis-based band delivering a raw, high-energy blend of heavy riffs, driving rhythms, and unfiltered intensity. Drawing from the darker edges of alternative, punk, and metal, their sound balances aggression with atmosphere and a visceral sense of momentum. Whether tearing through a crushing riff or locking into a relentless groove, Gauze brings an uncompromising energy to the stage. For fans of loud guitars, pounding drums, and music that hits hard, Gauze demands attention.

Heavy Music Night at Day Block Brewing

Get ready for a powerful night of metal, melodic hardcore, alternative rock, and heavy riffs as Inaara, VVakefield, Gradience, and Gauze take over the Tap Room at Day Block Brewing on Saturday, October 3rd, from 6–10 PM.

Inaara brings a dark, intense, and emotionally charged approach to modern metal. Their combination of crushing riffs, powerful rhythms, and story-driven songwriting draws from theatrical metal and emotionally raw post-hardcore. Expect an energetic performance packed with atmosphere and emotion.

Minneapolis melodic hardcore band VVakefield turns up the intensity with aggressive guitar work, driving drums, and melodic vocals. Their music balances the raw aggression of hardcore with memorable melodies, creating a sound built for an energetic live room.

Gradience brings a genre-spanning rock sound that blends hard rock, alternative, indie, and progressive influences. Their high-energy performances and melodic songwriting provide a dynamic change of pace while keeping the night loud and engaging.

Rounding out the lineup, Gauze delivers raw Minneapolis intensity through heavy riffs, relentless grooves, and driving rhythms. Pulling from alternative, punk, and metal, Gauze brings the kind of visceral energy that demands to be experienced live.

Between sets, enjoy the relaxed Day Block Brewing Tap Room atmosphere. Grab a fresh craft beer, order some food, hang out with friends, and take in an intimate night of live music surrounded by fellow fans. The combination of cold beer, good food, and four distinctly heavy bands makes this a perfect Saturday night for anyone who likes their music loud and energetic.

Social Pariah

Minnesota-based Social Pariah is a three-piece metal and grunge band bringing a heavy, raw edge to the local music scene. Influences including Alice in Chains, Pantera, Acid Bath, Crowbar, Soundgarden, and Mudvayne shape their aggressive yet melodic approach. With original music and a growing presence in the Minnesota scene, Social Pariah is pushing their sound in a heavier direction.

Taste of Vervain

Minneapolis-based Taste of Vervain delivers a crushing, progressive take on deathcore, combining heavy distortion, intricate rhythms, dissonant textures, and dynamic songwriting. The Twin Cities quartet—Justin, Kieran, Garrett, and Cade—pushes beyond straightforward brutality with a sound that balances aggression and atmosphere. Self-producing their music, the band released their six-song EP Until I Cease in 2025, showcasing their technical musicianship, intense vocals, and boundary-pushing approach to modern extreme metal.

Sensing Agony

Minnesota-based Sensing Agony is a post-hardcore band bringing raw intensity, melodic aggression, and emotionally charged energy to the Twin Cities scene. Founded by guitarist Kyan and drummer Ben before expanding with Shawn on bass and Jessica on vocals, the band draws from melodic hardcore and heavy alternative influences. Their powerful performances combine crushing instrumentation with dynamic vocals, showcased on singles including “House of Cards” and “Happy Song.” Sensing Agony is quickly establishing themselves as a band to watch.

A Martyrs Dilemma

Minnesota-based A Martyrs Dilemma delivers a crushing blend of modern metal and extreme heaviness, combining aggressive instrumentation, intense vocals, and dynamic songwriting. The band has built a presence in the Twin Cities metal scene through powerful live performances and uncompromising music. Their 2024 album REINVENTING HATRED showcases their relentless approach across seven tracks, including “Heavy Lies The Crown,” “Unhinged,” “Beyond God,” and “Villainized.” A Martyrs Dilemma continues pushing their sound into darker, heavier territory.

event.title: Front Porch | Triple Fiddle
event.description:
Front Porch

Described as “old time acid jazz punk rock barn burning bluegrass fusion that will have you jumping,” Front Porch independently released their first album “Shallow Grave” in the fall of 2023. Gaining attention across the U.S. with their energetic live shows, their performances highlight their skillful instrumentation, where foot stomping clawhammer banjo, ripping mandolin, guitar and fiddle melodies are at the forefront of their driving sound.

Front Porch has been nominated for bluegrass band of the year for the Arkansas Country Music Awards in 2024, 2025, and 2026, has headlined many festivals, and has supported artists such as Bela Fleck, Sierra Hull, Infamous Stringdusters, and Del McCoury. They are currently on tour supporting their sophomore album “Toolbox.”

Their most recent album highlights their continued growth as musicians and songwriters, where the band pushes the boundaries of American roots and bluegrass while creating their own unique sound. All four band members write songs for this album which creates a diversity of styles that reads as a cohesive collection. Guitarist John Henry pairs thoughtful storytelling with ripping guitar runs on his song, “Great Grandaddy’s Barn.” Bassist Cameron Keeling brings a traditional bluegrass feel with high lonesome harmonies on “Truer Words.” Mandolinist Alex Hawf brings dark jazz inspired melodies to his tune, “Skvader.” And banjo and fiddle player Petey Wesley brings an old time vibe with his song “Meet me in the Ground.”

Triple Fiddle 

Triple Fiddle is a Minneapolis-based fiddle ensemble featuring three powerhouse Minnesota fiddlers alongside guitarist Hannah Hendrickson. Known for soaring three-part fiddle harmonies and lush vocal arrangements, the group brings together an adventurous mix of honkytonk, western swing, bluegrass, jazz, classical chamber music, and Scandinavian folk. Their repertoire spans original songs, covers, and traditional fiddle tunes, creating a sound that is both deeply rooted and refreshingly modern. With years of experience performing throughout the Midwest, Triple Fiddle delivers a dynamic and captivating live experience that showcases the incredible possibilities of string-driven music.

Front Porch & Triple Fiddle at Day Block Brewing

Get ready for a night of high-energy American roots music, bluegrass, old-time, western swing, and genre-bending fiddle-driven sounds as Front Porch and special guests Triple Fiddle take over the Tap Room at Day Block Brewing on Friday, October 16th.

Described as “old time acid jazz punk rock barn burning bluegrass fusion that will have you jumping,” Front Porch brings a wild and energetic approach to bluegrass. Foot-stomping clawhammer banjo, ripping mandolin, guitar, fiddle, and soaring harmonies drive a sound that stretches well beyond traditional roots music. Currently touring behind their sophomore album Toolbox, Front Porch blends storytelling, instrumental fireworks, high-lonesome harmonies, dark jazz influences, and old-time melodies into a performance built to get the room moving.

Joining them is Triple Fiddle, a powerhouse Minnesota ensemble featuring three fiddlers and guitarist Hannah Hendrickson. Their music showcases soaring three-part fiddle harmonies, layered vocals, and intricate arrangements drawing from bluegrass, honkytonk, western swing, jazz, classical chamber music, and Scandinavian folk. The result is beautiful, energetic, and completely captivating.

The atmosphere at Day Block Brewing’s Tap Room will be relaxed, welcoming, and lively—a perfect setting for letting the music take over. Grab a cold craft beer, enjoy some food from the brewery, gather around with friends, and settle in for a night where traditional American music meets adventurous modern musicianship.

Whether you’re a longtime bluegrass fan or simply looking for something different, this is a night to tap your toes, stomp your feet, raise a pint, and enjoy some incredible live music.

event.description:
Dirty 930

Dirty-930 is a Mankato, Minnesota alternative garage band blending Midwest emo, indie punk, and raw, guitar-driven energy. Their music captures the messy transition from adolescence into adulthood, pairing catchy hooks with introspective, sometimes irreverent songwriting. With their 2026 album Throw Your Life Away, Dirty-930 delivers an honest, unfiltered collection of songs filled with youthful frustration, humor, melancholy, and existential uncertainty. Their sound is scrappy, emotional, and built for anyone navigating the chaos of growing up.

In Limbo

Minneapolis-based In Limbo is a rising local band bringing its own sound and energy to the Twin Cities music scene. With a growing presence on the Minneapolis live circuit and an active lineup of original music, In Limbo is quickly building a following through energetic performances and a strong connection with local audiences. Follow the band on Instagram for upcoming shows, new music, and updates from one of Minneapolis’ emerging independent acts.

One Singular Cigarette

One Singular Cigarette (OSC) is a Minnesota indie band crafting dreamy, atmospheric soundscapes with a nostalgic, wistful edge. Based in Mankato, the band blends lush textures and alternative influences into music that feels both modern and retro. OSC has become part of Minnesota’s growing independent music scene, performing at venues including Amsterdam Bar & Hall and sharing bills with fellow Midwest acts. Their hazy, immersive sound offers a distinctive take on indie music.

Lipstinger

Lipstinger is a high-flying, hot-rodded four-piece from rural Minnesota bringing unapologetic hard rock ’n’ roll to the stage. Drawing inspiration from the grit, swagger, and sleaze of ’70s and ’80s rock and metal, they deliver high-octane performances packed with driving guitar riffs, punchy rhythms, and soaring vocals. With raw energy and a head-turning live presence, Lipstinger is helping inject new life into Minnesota’s rock scene.

Dirty-930 closing out the night with a scrappy blend of Midwest emo, indie punk, and garage rock. Their guitar-driven sound pairs catchy hooks with honest, introspective songwriting, capturing the frustration, humor, melancholy, and uncertainty of growing up.

In Limbo brings their emerging Minneapolis sound to the stage with energetic performances and original music rooted in the Twin Cities independent scene. One Singular Cigarette follows with dreamy, atmospheric indie rock, creating hazy soundscapes filled with nostalgic textures and a wistful alternative edge.

Kicking things off, Lipstinger turns up the volume with high-octane hard rock ’n’ roll. Their four-piece sound draws from the grit and swagger of ’70s and ’80s rock and metal, delivering driving riffs, punchy rhythms, soaring vocals, and plenty of attitude.

The Day Block Tap Room provides the perfect intimate setting for a night that moves from emotional indie and garage rock to atmospheric soundscapes and full-throttle hard rock. event.description:
Buckls

Buckls is an artist from the Twin Cities playing melodic, power pop infused pop punk. Inspired by modern greats like Green Day, local legends like The Replacements and Husker Du, and singer-songwriters Bob Dylan and Jim Croce, he brings a catchy, old school charm to his songwriting that’ll stick in your head long after dancing in the pit.

Baltic Avenue Neighborhood Watch

Baltic Avenue Neighborhood Watch is a three piece punk rock band from Minneapolis, MN, featuring members of local favorites Couch Potato Masacre, King Sized Coffin, and Car Spiders. They write songs about every day life that the like to call, ‘sad and catchy.’

Economic Headwinds 

Economic Headwinds is a self described ‘corporate’ pop punk rock band based in St Paul who perform originals and covers. They’re for anyone sick of their job, loves cats, thinks bald is ok, and above all loves good music.

Punk Rock Night at Day Block Brewing

Get ready for a Saturday night of catchy hooks, loud guitars, cold beer, and melodic punk as Buckls, Baltic Avenue Neighborhood Watch, and Economic Headwinds take over the Tap Room at Day Block Brewing on Saturday, November 14th, from 7–10 PM.

Bring some friends, grab a table, order dinner from the kitchen, and settle in with a fresh craft beer before the volume goes up. The Tap Room provides the perfect setting for an intimate night of local music—part brewery hangout, part punk rock show, with plenty of energy once the bands hit the stage.

Buckls brings melodic, power-pop-infused pop punk with an old-school charm and a knack for songs that stick with you long after the show. Inspired by artists ranging from Green Day to Twin Cities legends The Replacements and Hüsker Dü, along with classic songwriters Bob Dylan and Jim Croce, Buckls blends catchy songwriting with enough energy to get the room moving.

Minneapolis trio Baltic Avenue Neighborhood Watch delivers what they call “sad and catchy” punk rock. Featuring members of local favorites Couch Potato Masacre, King Sized Coffin, and Car Spiders, the band turns everyday life into memorable, melodic punk songs with attitude, humor, and plenty of heart.

St. Paul’s Economic Headwinds rounds out the lineup with their self-described “corporate” pop punk rock. Mixing original music and covers, they’re here for anyone tired of their job, fond of cats, supportive of baldness, and—above all—ready for good music.

Three bands. Great food. Fresh beer. Catchy punk rock.

Day Block Brewing – Inside the Tap Room
Saturday, November 14th | 7–10 PM

Come early, grab a drink, support local music, and spend your Saturday night dancing, singing along, and enjoying the sounds of the Twin Cities punk scene.

Demon Alcohol ( A Tribute to Ozzy Osbourne )

Demon Alcohol is a Minnesota-based tribute to Ozzy Osbourne, bringing the legendary Prince of Darkness’ music to life with a hard-hitting live show. Covering Ozzy’s iconic solo career and classic heavy metal catalog, the band delivers crushing guitar riffs, powerful vocals, thunderous rhythms, and the unmistakable spirit of Ozzy’s music. From timeless hits to deeper cuts, Demon Alcohol celebrates the sound, energy, and theatrical attitude that have made Ozzy a defining figure in heavy metal for generations.

KISSin Time

KISSin Time is a Minnesota-based tribute band celebrating the music, spectacle, and larger-than-life rock ’n’ roll of KISS. Bringing the band’s iconic catalog to the stage, KISSin Time delivers powerful guitars, driving rhythms, soaring vocals, and the unmistakable attitude of classic KISS. With a high-energy performance built for rock fans, the band captures the excitement and theatrical spirit of a KISS concert while keeping the focus on the songs that made the legendary group a cornerstone of rock history.

Demon Alcohol – A Tribute to Ozzy Osbourne & KISSin Time

Saturday, November 28th | 6–10 PM | Day Block Brewing – Tap Room

Keep the Thanksgiving weekend rocking with two legendary tributes and one huge night of classic heavy rock! Demon Alcohol – A Tribute to Ozzy Osbourne and KISSin Time bring the music, attitude, and larger-than-life energy of two iconic acts to the intimate Day Block Brewing Tap Room.

Demon Alcohol delivers the dark, powerful side of Ozzy’s legendary catalog, featuring crushing guitar riffs, thunderous drums, powerful vocals, and classic heavy-metal anthems from Ozzy’s solo career. Expect plenty of headbanging, air guitar, and that unmistakable Ozzy attitude.

KISSin Time brings the spectacle and rock ’n’ roll swagger of KISS to the stage with powerful guitars, driving rhythms, soaring vocals, and the theatrical energy associated with one of rock’s most recognizable bands. Expect big songs, big personalities, and a live show designed to get the room moving.

The Day Block Tap Room will be turned into a rock ’n’ roll hangout for the evening. Grab a locally brewed Day Block beer or your favorite drink, enjoy some food from the kitchen, and settle in with friends for a night packed with classic rock, heavy metal, and plenty of volume.

The Tolerables

The Tolerables are a Minneapolis-based family pop-punk band formed in 2009, bringing high-energy hooks, driving guitars, and plenty of personality to the Twin Cities music scene. Inspired by bands like Paramore, Green Day, and MxPx, their music combines catchy songwriting with an energetic, playful live presence. Featuring brothers Luke, Tyler, and Jordan alongside Christie and Travis, The Tolerables are known for keeping audiences moving, singing along, and having a great time

Of The Orchard

Of The Orchard is a Minneapolis-based pop-rock band blending nostalgic ’90s and early-2000s rock with upbeat, hook-driven songwriting. Their sound combines catchy melodies, thoughtful lyrics, and influences from pop, alternative rock, folk, and pop-punk. With a knack for turning stories about growing up, relationships, and finding your place into infectious songs, Of The Orchard brings a fun, energetic Midwestern spirit to the stage. Their latest music showcases their signature “Sota Pop Rock” sound.

Sensing Agony

Sensing Agony is a Minnesota-based post-hardcore band delivering a powerful mix of melodic aggression, crushing instrumentation, and emotionally charged vocals. Founded by guitarist Kyan and drummer Ben before expanding with Shawn on bass and Jessica on vocals, the band draws from melodic hardcore and heavy alternative influences. Their music balances intense screams, dynamic melodies, heavy riffs, and breakdown-driven energy. With singles including “House of Cards” and “Happy Song,” Sensing Agony brings raw emotion and intensity to every performance.

Salt Fangs

Salt Fangs is a Minneapolis-based independent band bringing a fresh, energetic presence to the Twin Cities music scene. With a growing live profile and appearances alongside fellow local and regional artists, Salt Fangs delivers an engaging sound built for the stage. Their performances bring intensity, personality, and a contemporary edge to Minneapolis’ vibrant independent music community. The band continues to build momentum through live shows and new music, establishing their own place in the local scene.

The Tolerables • Of The Orchard • Sensing Agony • Salt Fangs

Salt Fangs opens the night, bringing a contemporary Minneapolis sound with plenty of energy, personality, and intensity. Their engaging live presence sets the tone for an evening built around discovering and celebrating local music.

Sensing Agony turns up the intensity with their emotionally charged post-hardcore sound. Expect crushing guitar riffs, powerful vocals, dynamic melodies, and breakdown-driven energy that brings a heavier edge to the night.

Of The Orchard follows with their upbeat “Sota Pop Rock,” blending nostalgic ’90s and early-2000s rock with pop, alternative, folk, and pop-punk influences. Catchy melodies and thoughtful lyrics make their set both energetic and approachable.

Headlining the night, The Tolerables bring their high-energy Minneapolis pop-punk sound to the Tap Room. Drawing inspiration from bands like Paramore, Green Day, and MxPx, they deliver driving guitars, huge hooks, sing-along moments, and a playful live presence designed to keep the room moving.

Enjoy the intimate Day Block Tap Room atmosphere while grabbing a locally brewed beer, your favorite drink, and some food from the kitchen. It’s the perfect Friday night setting to hang with friends, support Minnesota bands, and experience four different sides of the local music scene.

event.title: Seville Quarter Milers Run Club
event.description:
Meet at 5:30 PM | In Front of Seville Quarter

Run. Refuel. Repeat.

Lace up your running shoes and join the Seville Quarter Milers, Pensacola’s most fun and social midweek run! Whether you’re a seasoned runner or just starting out, all levels are welcome to hit the streets of Downtown Pensacola together.

Meet at 5:30 PM sharp in front of Seville Quarter for a relaxed group run through scenic downtown. No pressure, just good vibes, a great workout, and plenty of encouragement.

After the Run – It’s Time to Celebrate!

Head back to the End O’ the Alley Courtyard for a well-earned warm-down with:
• FREE post-run pasta to fuel your recovery
• Happy Hour drink specials
• Complimentary appetizers and a relaxed social atmosphere

Hang out with fellow runners, swap stories, make new friends, and enjoy one of Pensacola’s most welcoming running communities.
For more information on daily specials or upcoming events, call (850) 434-6211 or visit www.sevillequarter.com

event.title: Noche Tropical – Latin Night
event.description:
Presented by Latin Flavor Entertainment

Every Wednesday | 7:00 PM | Phineas Phogg’s

Wednesdays just got a whole lot hotter in Downtown Pensacola!

Seville Quarter and Latin Flavor Entertainment invite you to spice up your midweek routine with “Noche Tropical” Latin Night, held every Wednesday night in the iconic Phineas Phogg’s.

From 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM, get ready to move your feet with a vibrant Social Latin Dance experience featuring Salsa, Bachata, and Merengue, no partner required! Whether you’re a seasoned dancer or just getting started, this is the perfect night to feel the rhythm and connect with a fun, energetic crowd.

🎶 The night doesn’t stop there!
Once the social dancing wraps, it’s time for “FLAVOR TIME”, as DJ DavidC hits the decks and keeps the dance floor alive with a tropical mix of:
• Latin Pop
• Reggaeton
• Top 40 Latin Remixes
• Tropical Beats from across the globe

🍹 Drink Specials:
Enjoy refreshing Bacardi Rum Flavors Specials and tropical cocktails all night long to help you truly capture the spirit of the islands.

Whether you’re dancing the night away, sipping something smooth, or just soaking in the high-energy vibes, Noche Tropical is the #1 Latin Dance Party in Pensacola, a midweek fiesta you don’t want to miss!

Every Wednesday, Thursday, Friday & Saturday

Pensacola’s Original & Best College Night Experience

College Night is back and better than ever, only at Seville Quarter! For decades, Seville has been the Thursday night tradition for students across the Gulf Coast, and we’re still the #1 destination to kick off your weekend the right way.

Join hundreds of college students for a night of dancing, drinks, and unforgettable fun. Whether you’re rolling deep with your fraternity, sorority, or crew, this is the place to see and be seen.

event.title: Friday Happy Hour
event.description:
Make Happy Hour Great Again!

Join us every Friday as we wrap up the work week the only way we know how, with cold drinks, hot food, and great vibes in the End O’the Alley Courtyard at Seville Quarter!

We’re making Happy Hour Great Again with HUGE drink and food specials all day long. Happy Hour starting every week day at 11:00 AM and on Friday we are turning up the energy through the night. Whether you’re clocking out early or rallying the crew after work, Friday Happy Hour at Seville is the perfect place to catch up with friends, coworkers, or kick off your weekend with family.

Live Outdoor Cooking by Chef Jason Duckworth

Cold Drinks. Great People. Good Times.

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

Beginning Tuesday, October 6, Boots, Buckles & Boogie takes over Phineas Phogg’s at Seville Quarter with line dancing, partner dancing, Country Two-Step, Country Swing, and today’s hottest country music.

Dance instructor Dawn Alexander leads line and partner dance lessons from 7–9 p.m. Whether you are learning your first steps or fine-tuning your footwork, Dawn will have you boot-scootin’ with confidence in no time.

After the lessons, Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie takes over, playing country-dance favorites all night long on Boss Phogg’s dance floor.

With a true honky-tonk atmosphere andPensacola’s #1 dance floor, Phineas Phogg’s is the perfect place for beginners, experienced dancers, couples, singles, and groups of friends to gather, dance, and show off their moves.

The music will be playing, the crowd will be ready, and Boss Phogg’s dance floor will be calling your name!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.
